findings.title: Feature and decision-context provenance is caller-self-attested
evidence: The request supplies the feature schema under a constant schema version.
Feature source, availability and observed_at are supplied in the same untrusted row as the value.
The name denylist can reject explicit outcome/future tokens but cannot prove the semantics of an innocently renamed future-derived feature.

Regime is accepted as a string, sector is omitted from the training row, and provider binding checks a contract-version string plus coarse freshness rather than immutable decision-time source evidence.
A consistently supplied but invalid cohort/sample pairing is not checked against a closed cohort-to-sample mapping.
findings.impact: Leakage or context relabeling can enter a self-consistent dataset and produce a trainable artifact while retaining canonical-looking digests.
findings.required_remediation: Use a separately trusted, versioned feature registry and bind every feature/context value to immutable decision-time capture evidence, source timestamp, producer version and cohort/sample policy.

findings.title: Walk-forward isolation does not bind scan, opportunity-set or outcome-overlap groups
evidence: Split construction groups rows by decision_day and checks canonical decision identity disjointness only.
The same opportunity-set identity and digest can be present on both sides of a split if its rows carry different days.
No scan identity, evaluator-input identity, outcome completion timestamp or overlap-group identity participates in the split gate.
Caller-supplied purge_days and embargo_days are not derived from or checked against actual outcome intervals and trading-session timestamps.
findings.impact: Related candidates or overlapping labels can cross the train/test boundary and inflate out-of-sample evidence.
findings.required_remediation: Introduce canonical split-group and outcome-interval evidence, keep complete scan/opportunity groups together, and derive purge/embargo eligibility from actual timestamped horizons.

findings.title: Deterministic rebuild has no trusted input anchor
evidence: Result verification recomputes the expected result from the caller-supplied request.
There is no frozen training-input manifest, registry/root digest or upstream canonical evidence digest verified outside that request.
A caller can change features, labels, lineage or versions and then recompute every internal dataset/model/result digest; verification accepts the new self-consistent pair.
findings.impact: The implementation detects result-only tampering but cannot detect self-consistent substitution of the training evidence.
findings.required_remediation: Bind training to an external trusted dataset manifest/root derived from frozen Action 664–666 evidence and require that anchor before dataset construction and result verification.

findings.title: Extreme finite inputs can escape the structured status contract
evidence: Input validation accepts every finite number, including values large enough to overflow sums, variances or gradients.
The rounding guard throws on a non-finite intermediate instead of returning non_reproducible.
findings.impact: A fixture run can terminate with an exception instead of one of the four documented result statuses.
findings.required_remediation: Add bounded numeric-domain contracts and convert all numerical failures into deterministic non_reproducible diagnostics.

findings.title: Disabled mode still clones the complete request
evidence: The disabled path avoids the injected trainer but performs structuredClone(request) and reads request.rows.length.
findings.impact: Default-off prevents training but does not literally perform zero input processing and can pay memory cost for a large fixture.
findings.required_remediation: Return a fixed disabled result before cloning or traversing the request.

findings.title: Logistic local contributions are not explicitly typed as log-odds
evidence: Logistic contributions are coefficient times standardized feature and reconstruct the linear predictor correctly.
The output names the reconstructed value prediction_scale_value without a versioned log_odds scale discriminator.
findings.impact: A downstream offline consumer could misread additive log-odds contributions as additive probability changes.
findings.required_remediation: Add an explicit attribution scale contract distinguishing logistic log_odds from linear canonical_r.

findings.title: Correlated-feature attribution caveat is implicit rather than explicit
evidence: Documentation rejects causal interpretation and mentions confounding and regime drift, but does not explicitly state coefficient and ablation instability under correlated features.
findings.impact: Interpretation guidance is slightly less precise for multicollinear inputs.
findings.required_remediation: Name correlated-feature attribution instability explicitly in the contract documentation.
